senses.definition: One who disclaims, disowns, or renounces.
A public disavowal, as of responsibility, pretensions, claims, opinions, etc.

translations.word: cláusula de renuncia a la imputabilidad

senses.definition: (law) A denial, disavowal, or renunciation, as of a title, claim, interest, estate, or trust; relinquishment or waiver of an interest or estate.

quotes.text: Subject to the provisions of this section, any person who, after the commencement of this Act, succeeds to a peerage in the peerage of England, Scotland, Great Britain or the United Kingdom may, by an instrument of disclaimer delivered to the Lord Chancellor within the period prescribed by this Act, disclaim that peerage for his life.
quotes.reference: 1963, Parliament of the United Kingdom, “section 1(1)”, in Peerage Act 1963ᵂⁱᵏⁱˢᵒᵘʳᶜᵉ, page 1:

senses.definition: (proscribed) A disclosure of an interest, relationship, or the like.

quotes.text: It interviewed, among others, the director of Vasant Valley School, owned by the same family that part-owns Mail Today. No disclaimer was carried stating as much.
quotes.reference: May 10 2012, Anant Rangaswami, “No need for regulation in media – it’s happening by itself”, in Firstpost:

quotes.text: Though the fact that the two men do business together was disclosed on air, a recent op-ed penned by Lako and published on the Hannity show’s website had no such disclaimer.

senses.definition: (transitive, informal) To disclaim or disavow, as by appending a legal disclaimer.
